title.en: Meta Hyperion (Beignet) Data Center Financing - Case Facts
title.zh: Meta Hyperion（Beignet）数据中心融资——案例事实

description.en: All case facts on the Meta/Blue Owl Hyperion transaction from Section IV and footnotes 3, 4, 7 plus Figure 2 notes: ~2.0 GW capacity and ~$30B total investment (≈$15M/MW excl. IT equipment), 80% equity sale to Blue Owl for ≈$2.5B, the Beignet JV's $27B October 2025 bond (S&P A+, largest single IG corporate bond in U.S. history), ~90% project debt/asset and 1.12x DSCR, the bankruptcy-remote SPV chain (Laidley LLC / Project Beignet Holdings LLC / Iris Crossing LLC / Beignet Investor LLC / Entergy Louisiana PPA with three gas-fired units), five 4-year leases 2029-2049 with per-renewal termination, asset sale and Meta residual value guarantee, GAAP non-recognition before effectiveness, the 6.58% issuance yield (>=100bp over Meta unsecured, >$5B lifetime extra interest), Meta's own year-end 2025 leverage (25% book / 4% market) and $130B OCF covering 2026 debt service >=18x, and the Sopaipilla template case.
description.zh: Section IV 与脚注 3、4、7 及图 2 注释中 Meta/Blue Owl Hyperion 交易的全部案例事实：约 2.0 GW 容量、总投资约 300 亿美元（约合 1500 万美元/MW，不含 IT 设备）、向 Blue Owl 出售 80% 股权约 25 亿美元、合资公司 Beignet 于 2025 年 10 月发行 270 亿美元债券（S&P A+，美国史上最大单笔投资级公司债）、项目负债/资产约 90%、DSCR 1.12x、破产隔离 SPV 链条（Laidley LLC / Project Beignet Holdings LLC / Meta 经 Iris Crossing LLC 持 20% / Blue Owl 经 Beignet Investor LLC / 与 Entergy Louisiana 的 PPA 及三台燃气机组）、2029-2049 年五段各 4 年租约及逐节点终止权、资产出售与 Meta 残值担保、生效前 GAAP 不入表、6.58% 发行收益率（高于 Meta 同类无担保债至少 100bp、全周期多付超 50 亿美元利息）、Meta 2025 年末自身杠杆（账面 25%/市值 4%）及 1300 亿美元经营现金流对 2026 年债务偿付至少 18 倍覆盖，以及模板案例 Sopaipilla。

notes: Printed page = PDF page - 2; Section IV spans printed pp. 8-11 (PDF 10-13).

Financing is organized through a network of bankruptcy-remote special-purpose vehicles that issue debt backed by contractual claims on future lease payments; the structure 'isolates the project from Meta's broader corporate balance sheet and enhances creditor protection, but it also makes ultimate exposures more difficult to trace' (Section IV, PDF p.11).

The residual value guarantee 'gives Meta operational flexibility while preserving much of the long-duration credit support that lenders would otherwise obtain from a conventional long-term lease'; 'Meta's reported leverage therefore understates the economic obligations embedded in the contract' (Section IV, PDF p.11).

Economic rationale: 'not cheaper financing, but preservation of an asset-light corporate profile'; Meta 'avoids adding the full amount of the associated assets and debt to its own balance sheet' (Section IV, PDF pp.12-13).
Bondholders lack a direct claim on Meta's balance sheet; 'the bonds' longer duration and specialized private-placement structure also contribute to the interest premium' (Section IV, PDF p.13).
Template features: 'investment-grade tenant credit, high project-level leverage, bankruptcy-remote entities, lease optionality, and a residual value guarantee' (Section IV, PDF p.13).
Figure 2 sources cited by the paper: Standard & Poor's pre-sale report; Entergy 2025 Form 10-K (PDF p.12).
The paper states the A+ rating is 'one notch below Meta's own corporate credit rating' but does not state Meta's own letter rating.
Blue Owl's JV share is not separately stated in Figure 2 notes; the 80% comes from the stake-sale sentence in Section IV (PDF p.10).
'project_asset_value' ($30B, PDF p.11) and 'total_investment' ($30B, PDF p.10) refer to the same project amount as discussed in two sentences.

provenance.quote_en: The project involves approximately 2.0 GW of capacity and a total investment of about $30 billion, making it one of the largest single data center developments to date.
This corresponds to about $15 million per MW, broadly consistent with our estimate of $11 million per MW for the facility plus additional power-infrastructure costs.
The figure excludes IT equipment, which Meta will finance separately as the tenant.
Meta initially owned the project outright but subsequently sold an 80 percent equity stake to Blue Owl for approximately $2.5 billion.
The resulting joint venture, Beignet, then raised $27 billion of external debt in October 2025.
The debt was rated A+ by Standard & Poor’s, one notch below Meta’s own corporate credit rating, and represented the largest individual investment-grade corporate debt issuance in U.S. history.
Beignet financed roughly $27 billion of the $30 billion asset value with debt, implying a debt-to-asset ratio of about 90 percent.
The debt service coverage ratio is only 1.12×.
Meta’s own year-end 2025 leverage ratio was approximately 25 percent using book equity and just 4 percent using market equity.
Meta’s operating cash flow of $130 billion is at least 18× its 2026 debt service.
Meta addresses this tension through a sequence of five four-year leases beginning in 2029 and extending through the bond’s 2049 maturity.
At each renewal date, Meta may terminate the lease for some or all of the Hyperion campus.
If it does so, the affected assets are offered for sale, and Meta must cover any shortfall between the sale proceeds and a contractually specified minimum value.
Under current GAAP rules, Meta does not recognize the future lease obligations nor the residual value guarantee on its balance sheet before the relevant lease or guarantee becomes effective
Laidley LLC owns the datacenter campus, which is funded by its subsidiary Project Beignet Holdings LLC.
The latter is owned in Joint Venture for 20% by Meta, through Iris Crossing LLC, and by Blue Owl, through Beignet Investor LLC.
Laidley enters in a Power Purchase Agreement with Entergy Louisiana, which will develop three gas-fired generating units.
Beignet’s debt was issued at a yield of 6.58%, at least 100 basis points above the rate Meta likely would have paid on comparable unsecured corporate debt at the time of issuance.
Over the life of the financing, that spread implies more than $5 billion of additional interest expense for Beignet, a cost which is ultimately reflected in Meta’s lease payments.
The economic rationale for Meta is therefore not cheaper financing, but preservation of an asset-light corporate profile.
Beignet bondholders receive a higher interest rate because they do not have a direct claim on Meta’s balance sheet.
The Hyperion transaction may therefore provide a template for future data center financings.
Indeed, the 960MW Sopaipilla datacenter project in El Paso, TX, a joint venture of Meta and Blackrock, follows a nearly identical structure.
Sopaipilla investor issued $12.3 billion in A+-rated bonds in July 2026.
